newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris speed limits cut to counter pollution.
newsitem.headline: Paris speed limits cut to counter pollution.

text.p: Police decreed stricter speed limits in the Paris area on Tuesday in a bid to counter high pollution levels as drivers faced snarl-ups because of a demonstration by Renault car workers.
Authorities lowered the limit from 80 kph (50 mph) to 60 kmh (37 mph) on the capital's ring road, and from 70 kph (44 mph) to 50 kph (30 mph) on express riverbank roads through the city.

Drivers on motorways and expressways in the Ile-de-France area around Paris will also have to slow down by 20 kph (12 mph) after air pollution reached high levels on Monday, chiefly because of car exhaust fumes and the lack of wind.
Paris mayor Jean Tiberi said residential parking would be free of charge on Tuesday to encourage locals to use buses and the underground metro railway until pollution levels return to normal.

Organisers expect more than 10,000 French, Belgian, Spanish and Italian demonstrators to take part in a march on part of Paris's ring road towards Renault's headquarters at Boulogne-Billancourt to protest at the firm's plans to axe some 6,000 jobs in Europe.
